rationale: Inferred from the brief: a contemporary software-house website with service discovery, a product shop, cart and checkout, company information, and contact workflows.

questions.question: Which language should power the React frontend?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed React development with stronger maintainability and editor support.

questions.rationale: TypeScript is the best fit for a multi-page storefront, cart state, checkout flows, and reusable service components.

questions.question: Which React framework and UI approach should the frontend use?

options.label: Next.js with Fluent UI v9
options.description: Production React framework with routing, server rendering options, and a polished enterprise component library.

options.label: Vite React with Fluent UI v9
options.description: Fast client-rendered React application with explicit routing and build configuration.

questions.rationale: Next.js supports a strong content and commerce experience while Fluent UI v9 provides consistent accessible primitives.

questions.question: Which language should power the backend API?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Shared language across the React frontend and commerce API.

options.label: Python
options.description: Flexible backend option with a broad web ecosystem.

questions.rationale: TypeScript keeps the product, cart, checkout, contact, and service inquiry contracts aligned across the stack.

questions.question: Which backend framework should expose catalog, checkout, contact, and service inquiry APIs?

options.label: Next.js Route Handlers
options.description: Co-located typed API routes for the Next.js application.

options.label: NestJS
options.description: Structured TypeScript API with a dedicated service architecture.

questions.rationale: Co-located route handlers minimize operational complexity for this initial marketing and commerce application.

sharedQuestions.question: Which data stores does the application need?

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Products, service offerings, orders, checkout records, and contact inquiries.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Product imagery, downloadable assets, and service media.

options.label: Redis
options.description: Optional caching or short-lived cart/session data.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only static or in-memory data; exclusive choice.

sharedQuestions.rationale: The shop and checkout require durable order and catalog data, while the product experience needs media storage.

sharedQuestions.question: Should users sign in to access application API features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Customers and/or staff sign in to access protected API features.

options.label: No
options.description: Public browsing and guest checkout are available without sign-in.

sharedQuestions.rationale: Guest checkout keeps the first release focused and reduces friction; staff administration can be added behind a later protected surface.
